The issue page passes its member list and `createCommentAction` to `CommentComposer` in [page.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/[issueNumber]/page.tsx). As the user types, `MentionTextarea` calls `resolveMentions` and reports the body and resolved user IDs to the composer. The composer stores both, validates them with `createCommentSchema`, and submits them through the action. Autocomplete is optional: typing a complete handle also invokes resolution.

In [mentions.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/lib/mentions.ts), `extractMentions` ignores fenced and inline code, recognizes handles at the start of the body or after allowed whitespace or punctuation, lowercases them, and removes duplicates. `handleOf` defines a handle as the lowercase local part of a member’s email. `resolveMentions` maps those handles to `MemberWithUser.userId`; unknown handles are dropped.

[create-comment.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts) validates and authorizes the request, applies rate limiting, and calls `createComment` in [comment-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/server/services/comment-service.ts). That service checks organization scope, issue permissions and archival state, and rate limits again. Its `resolveMentionedUsers` loads the first 100 non-archived organization members through `listMembers`, resolves the body again, and unions those IDs with client-provided IDs that appear in that same member list. Thus the server can find a typed handle independently of the client, but members outside that first page cannot be resolved there. It does not require a retained client ID to appear in the body.

`createComment` passes the resulting `mentionedUserIds` to `insertComment` in [comment-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/server/repositories/comment-repository.ts), which stores the array as JSON on the comment. It then emits `comment.created` with the same list, along with the organization, actor, issue and comment IDs. The payload is defined by `TaskflowEventMap` in [event.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/types/event.ts); the list in that event is what carries the recipients to fan-out.

At server startup, [instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/instrumentation.ts) loads the event registry, whose import of [notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/server/services/notification-service.ts) runs `registerFanOut`. Its `comment.created` subscriber first calls `notify` for the issue author and assignee as `comment_created` watchers, then calls it for `mentionedUserIds` as `comment_mention`. A mentioned watcher can therefore receive both kinds. `emit` in [event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/lib/event-bus.ts) awaits subscribers but isolates their failures, so a successful comment write does not guarantee a successful notification.

For each distinct mention recipient, `notify` skips the actor and retrieves that user’s per-organization, per-kind preference with `getPreference`. `resolveChannels` selects `in_app` when `inApp` is true, and `email` when `email` is true and either `digestOnly` is false or the `digest_email` flag is enabled. With no preference row, it defaults to both channels. If neither is selected, `notify` inserts nothing; otherwise `insertNotifications` in [notification-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts) writes one unread row containing the selected channels.

There are two consequential implementation details in that last step. First, the inbox page calls `listNotifications`, whose repository query filters by organization and recipient but **does not filter by channel**. An email-only row therefore also appears in the in-app inbox. Second, selecting `email` on a row does **not** itself send an immediate mention email: `notify` only inserts the row. The separate `runDigestEmailJob` in [digest-email-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts) can collect unread rows for digest subscribers when the flag and schedule allow it, render a digest and call `sendEmail`. That digest collection does not filter rows by their channels or kind. Finally, `sendEmail` in [email-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/8fd2abe0-bdf7-49e8-aa04-0b5b50476910/src/server/services/email-service.ts) logs the send; this application has no outbound mail transport.
